hypotheses.justification:
For a Noetherian ring R, `AdicCompletion I R` is flat over R. The instance `AdicCompletion.flat_of_isNoetherian` at line 378 of the same file proves this. Flatness makes `lTensor (AdicCompletion I R) f` injective for every injective `f`, with no finiteness condition on M or N. The lemma for this is `Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap` in Mathlib/RingTheory/Flat/Basic.lean. As a function, `AlgebraTensorModule.map LinearMap.id f` is the same map as `f.lTensor _`; both agree on pure tensors.

The flatness instance is currently proved from this very lemma, so the order needs care, but there is no real circularity. The flatness proof only uses the lemma for `J.subtype : J → R` with J an ideal. Both `J` and `R` are finite R-modules when R is Noetherian, and both live in universe u. So the new proof goes as follows. First prove flatness inside the proof: use `Module.Flat.iff_lTensor_injective'`, then the current argument (`tensor_map_id_left_eq_map` and `map_injective`) with M := J and N := R. Then apply `lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap` to `f` and `hf`. This never uses `Module.Finite R N`. The only remaining hypotheses needed are `[IsNoetherianRing R]` and `hf`. The same argument also removes `[Module.Finite R M]`, so the two can be deleted together.

The argument is the same as for `[Module.Finite R N]`. Since R is Noetherian, `AdicCompletion I R` is flat over R. This flatness can be proved inside the proof from the existing finite case: use `Module.Flat.iff_lTensor_injective'` with the inclusion of an ideal J into R, both finite over the Noetherian R, together with `tensor_map_id_left_eq_map` and `map_injective`. Then `Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap` gives injectivity of `f.lTensor (AdicCompletion I R)`, which as a function equals `AlgebraTensorModule.map LinearMap.id f`. This holds for any injective `f`, with no finiteness condition on M. Both finiteness hypotheses can be deleted, separately or together.
